# Will it fit, will it boot, will it answer? Current open models on rented GPUs

<!-- Draft. The tables between findings markers are generated by
scripts/cohort_findings.py from the stored records, cohort/modern-models.json
and the GPU-free predictions, and checked by tests/unit/test_cohort_findings.py;
never edit them by hand. The prose is updated here as each group of runs
lands; the owner rewrites it. This post stays `draft: true` until the owner
publishes it. The first cohort's post (phase-1b-cohort-findings.md) stays as
it is. -->

Before you rent GPUs for a new open model, you want three answers: will it
fit, will it boot, and will it answer. Apron gives the first one before any
GPU is rented, and the other two with a single boot. If the boot fails, it
reads the error, changes the plan and boots again. This post runs it on
open models people download today: gpt-oss, GLM, Gemma 4, Qwen 3.x, MiniMax,
DeepSeek and Kimi, from one GPU up to eight.

## The models, and what Apron said before renting a GPU

Twelve models in four groups, chosen by downloads and by what they need:
one GPU with an architecture Apron already models (A); one GPU with an
attention type it does not model yet (B); two to four GPUs (C); eight GPUs
(D). "Before any GPU" is Apron's plan from the model's files alone: the
config and the tensor headers on the Hub. It downloads no weights and rents
no GPU.

**"Unknown" is an answer, not a gap in the table.** Qwen 3.6 and 3.8,
Nemotron 3 and Gemma 4 mix ordinary attention with state that works
differently (Mamba or linear attention), or keep the text model inside a
multimodal config. vLLM lists 25 such hybrid model classes. Apron says
"unknown" for them rather than guess. Its first answer for Nemotron 3 was a
confident number, and that number would have been wrong.

**The GPU-free pass found three mistakes of ours** before any money was
spent. Each is fixed, and each is in the run notebook:

- a model split across several GPUs was sized as if it sat on one;
- hybrid models got an estimate for ordinary attention;
- the check that asks "would vLLM load these tensors?" refused every large
  mixture-of-experts model. It did not know the tensors the model itself
  owns, such as the expert router's bias. It now refuses a tensor only when
  vLLM's source names it nowhere. That still catches the case it was built
  for: FPQuant checkpoints that no vLLM since 0.23 can load.

## Not paying a GPU to download

A 700 GB model downloaded on eight H200s ($37/hour) costs money before
anything runs. Apron now stages the weights first. A CPU pod in the same
datacenter downloads them onto a network volume and verifies every file.
Then the GPU pod attaches that volume and only loads. The table shows,
per boot, where the pod's time went.

## When it broke

Six deliberately broken plans, one per kind of failure, from the first
cohort. Apron fixed each one and re-ran the same tasks. New failures on the
modern models will be added here as they happen.

<!-- findings:fixes -->
| Failure | Broken plan | vLLM error from | What Apron changed | Fixed plan booted | Tasks passed | SLO passed | Result | Record |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Weights do not fit the GPU | Qwen/Qwen3-14B on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `model_executor/layers/linear.py:192` | GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 → NVIDIA RTX A6000 | yes | yes | yes | Fixed | `1220f4b5d596eaa3` |
| 2. No room for the KV cache | Qwen/Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:879` | max_model_len: 40960 → 32640 | yes | yes | yes | Fixed | `1220e8f6ea8e7da0` |
| 3. Context length above the model's limit | mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `config/model.py:2502` | max_model_len: 999999 → 32768 | yes | yes | yes | Fixed | `12207f1e236c341a` |
| 4. float16 not supported by the model | google/gemma-2-2b-it on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 | `config/model.py:2262` | dtype: float16 → bfloat16 | yes | yes | yes | Fixed | `122038df2ccafa66` |
| 5. Tensor parallelism does not divide the heads | Qwen/Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB | `config/model.py:1414` | tensor parallel: 3 → 2 | yes | yes | yes | Fixed | `12208faa3f0af819` |
| 6. Quantization needs a newer GPU | ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3-8B-FPQuant-RTN-MXFP4 on NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 | `config/vllm.py:791` | model: ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3-8B-FPQuant-RTN-MXFP4 → Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ | yes | yes | yes | Fixed | `12201e071813c808` |
<!-- /findings:fixes -->

## Limits

- One provider (RunPod, Secure cloud). One measurement per point unless a
  table says otherwise.
- The task check is three short questions scored by exact match. It shows
  whether a model answers at all, not how good it is.
- The GPU is chosen by what is in stock in a datacenter that can hold the
  weights, so a model may run on a different GPU than proposed. The table
  shows the GPU it actually ran on.
- The H200's memory size in Apron's table is not yet confirmed on a pod.

## What's next, and a question

Group A runs first, then B once Apron models hybrid attention, then C and D.
Results land in this post and in the public records as they arrive. Which
model on which GPU should we run next? Answer in
[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/mondegreens/apron/discussions).
